# For municipalities and government

::: {.lead}
Many public services are allocated not by price but through applications, priorities and waiting lists. Well-designed procedures ensure that available places are fully used, preferences are met as far as possible and decisions remain transparent.
:::
:::

## How we work together

```{=html}
<ol class="timeline">
<li><strong>Initial conversation.</strong> Which places are allocated, under which rules, and where the problems lie.</li>
<li><strong>Analysis.</strong> Evaluation of past allocation data and simulation of alternative rules.</li>
<li><strong>Rule design.</strong> Priorities, quotas and special cases such as siblings, agreed with providers and within the legal framework.</li>
<li><strong>Implementation and evaluation.</strong> Introduction, usually as a pilot first, with accompanying evaluation.</li>
</ol>
```

Research and evaluation take place at Pforzheim University and ZEW. Software for day-to-day operation is provided by MatchingTools GmbH.
